subject: Cloud Computing
title: Public, Private, and Hybrid Clouds
description: A fast breakdown of Public, Private, and Hybrid Clouds for builders.

hook.text: Not all clouds are created equal. Some are open to everyone, others are locked behind firewalls.

buildup.text: Public cloud is shared infrastructure from AWS, Azure, or Google — open to any paying customer.

discovery.text: Private cloud runs on hardware dedicated to one organization, often inside their own building.

twist.text: Most large companies use hybrid: sensitive data on private cloud, everything else on public.

climax.text: Hybrid sounds ideal, but connecting two clouds securely is one of the hardest problems in IT.

punchline.text: Public is easy. Private is safe. Hybrid is both — and hard.

quiz.question: What is a hybrid cloud?
options: A combination of public and private cloud working together
A cloud that only operates during certain hours
A cloud service that works without an internet connection

details.summary: Public clouds share infrastructure among all customers over the internet. Private clouds dedicate infrastructure to a single organization. Hybrid clouds connect both, allowing workloads to move between them. Most enterprises today use a hybrid approach to balance flexibility, cost, and control.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing the right cloud deployment model affects security, compliance, cost, and operational complexity. Most organizations evolve toward hybrid strategies that optimize each workload's placement.
takeaways: Public clouds offer shared infrastructure at the lowest cost
Private clouds provide dedicated resources and full control
Hybrid approaches combine both for optimal workload placement

faq.question: When would you choose private over public cloud?
faq.answer: Private cloud suits workloads with strict regulatory requirements, data sovereignty constraints, consistent high utilization, or specialized hardware needs. Organizations in healthcare, finance, and government often use private cloud for sensitive workloads while using public cloud for others.

faq.question: What makes hybrid cloud challenging?
faq.answer: Hybrid requires networking between environments, consistent security policies across both, data synchronization, and tools that work in both. Managing two different environments adds operational complexity. Technologies like Kubernetes help by providing a consistent platform across both.
